claim: Angle is the classic dominance lever: the tilt of the lens relative to the subject. Low makes a figure monumental, high makes them small and observed, and dutch says the world itself is off its axis.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: worm's-eye view, extreme low angle, from below

review.issue: birds_eye ("bird's-eye view, from far above") and top_down ("top-down view, from directly above") are the same instruction in two phrasings and will render as one picture; both also duplicate cam.height.overhead/aerial. worms_eye ("worm's-eye view, extreme low angle, from below") differs from low ("from below, low angle") only by intensifiers the model largely ignores.
review.fix: Keep level / low / high / dutch as the load-bearing four plus one overhead extreme, and delete the twin. Assign overhead ownership to exactly one card (angle or height, not both).
